items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: I think from a standpoint of musical quality, that the sessions that Wiggs and Harry Shields and Tom Brown made together are certainly among the very greatest of jazz recordings.

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah, I'm just wondering how you fit Wiggs into something like this.

Well, how I fit Wiggs in, I think that Wiggs, from a standpoint of band cornet, that is as a jazz band cornetist, is the best jazz band cornetist that I ever heard. That is that he plays better lead, he plays proper lead, makes it easier to put a band together. And you know, to my way of thinking, was the ideal jazz band trumpet player. I also feel that the quality of the music played by Wiggs' bands in the revival is at least as good, and in many cases better, than most of the stuff that we revere as the…

Yeah, I find that, in a way, how many, I find this hard to sort out in my mind, because I'm trying to sort out all the different Wiggs's in my mind, and your opinion of the different Wiggs's, our opinions.
